narrative.northStar: Read in daylight, recognize in forest, act on one green — and let amber only ever whisper.
narrative.overview:
Sage-light surfaces carry the reading. Deep forest green (the Instagram color) carries the identity, in tiles and bands. One action green carries every clickable primary action and nothing else. Amber is a rare highlight, never an action. If a new element makes any of these jobs ambiguous, its color is wrong.

Brand: Mitec (میتک), a studio for websites and digital solutions (online services, CRM, automation, data analytics, support). Target market: Iran. Language: Persian, RTL (`<html lang="fa" dir="rtl">`). Latin appears only in brand names and the `mitec.team` wordmark. Font: Vazirmatn (weights 400 / 500 / 700 / 800). Fallback: `Tahoma, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`. Numerals: use Persian digits (۰–۹) in UI copy and stats. Visual link: the site must feel like the same brand as the Instagram page (dark green `#12312A` posts, mint `#57B79A`, amber `#E0A25C`, subtle grid texture, device mockups on green).
keyCharacteristics: Deep forest green (the Instagram color) carries the identity, in tiles and bands.
One action green carries every clickable primary action and nothing else.
Amber is a rare highlight, never an action.

rules.name: No navy or blue
rules.body: No navy or blue anywhere, except the `info` status token. Client content is not UI: a project's screenshots, and in Work the ambient backdrop made from them, keep the client's own colours (E2's blue). Those colours never become a token or touch anything we draw.

rules.name: Components use semantic tokens only
rules.body: Components use semantic tokens only (`--color-*`). Primitives (`--green-600`, `--sage-200`…) appear only in the token file.

rules.name: One solid primary button per viewport
rules.body: One solid primary button per viewport , and at most one per section.

rules.name: Action green (`--color-cta`) is only for clickable things
rules.body: Action green (`--color-cta`) is only for clickable things. Stats, chart bars, decorative icons and headings are never action green.

rules.name: Never put mint `#57B79A` or amber `#E0A25C` text on light backgrounds
rules.body: Never put mint `#57B79A` or amber `#E0A25C` text on light backgrounds. They fail contrast (2.43:1 and 2.07:1).

rules.name: Never use pure `#FFFFFF`
rules.body: Never use pure `#FFFFFF` as the page background or as text on dark. Use `#F5F7F4` for the page and `#F1F5F2` for text on dark.

rules.name: Every dark area must set `data-surface="dark"`
rules.body: Every dark area must set `data-surface="dark"`. Never hand-pick colors inside a dark area.

rules.name: Forms are always on light surfaces
rules.body: Forms are always on light surfaces.

rules.name: No gradients, glows or amber on buttons
rules.body: No gradients, glows or amber on buttons.

rules.name: No third accent hue
rules.body: No third accent hue. The palette is green + sage + amber, plus status colors.

rules.name: Hierarchy is never color alone
rules.body: Hierarchy is never color alone. Always pair it with size and weight.

rules.name: Persian: treat 4
rules.body: Persian: treat 4.5:1 as the minimum even for large text under 24px. Thin joins and dots lose definition faster than Latin.

rules.name: Line-height ≥ 1
rules.body: Line-height ≥ 1.8 for Persian body text.

rules.name: Letter-spacing 0 on Persian text, headings and eyebrows included (`--ls-*` are 0)
rules.body: Letter-spacing 0 on Persian text, headings and eyebrows included (`--ls-*` are 0). Persian is a joined script: any tracking, positive or negative, opens gaps in the joins. Latin wordmarks may keep theirs.

rules.name: Opt-in
rules.body: Opt-in. Every motion rule is scoped to `html.motion`, set only when the visitor has not asked for reduced motion (and is not in forced colours). Without it — reduced motion, no JS, forced colours — the page is the plain static document with everything visible and complete: no pinning, no scrubbing, no reveals, no smooth scrolling.

rules.name: Transform and opacity only, per frame
rules.body: Transform and opacity only, per frame. Scroll-linked effects never animate width/height/position, `clip-path`, masks, filters, shadows or background position per frame. Masks and geometry are set on resize. Class or attribute flips (a nav switching surface, a spotlight moving) happen only when state changes, and their CSS transitions do the rest.

rules.name: One engine
rules.body: One engine. One `requestAnimationFrame` loop and one passive scroll listener (`src/scripts/motion/engine.js`) serve every scroll-linked effect; layout is read only in `measure()` (resize, load, font swap), never in the loop. Off-screen effects are skipped.

rules.name: One pinned scene per page
rules.body: One pinned scene per page. On the home page that is the portal hero; everything after it scrolls normally.

rules.name: Pointer lean is decoration only
rules.body: Pointer lean is decoration only. The hero's float cards lean up to 14px toward a fine pointer, eased on the engine; never on touch, in the lite scene or without motion, and they are gone once the dive starts.

rules.name: Reversible
rules.body: Reversible. Scroll-linked motion is a pure function of scroll position, so scrolling back replays it in reverse. No one-shot triggers inside a scene.

rules.name: Reveal once, calmly
rules.body: Reveal once, calmly. Entrances play once as a section arrives: rise 20–28px and fade, 600–700ms `--ease-entrance`, 60–90ms stagger. Content that keyboard focus reaches shows at once.

rules.name: Words, never characters
rules.body: Words, never characters. Persian text may reveal by whole words or phrases (ZWNJ-joined words stay whole), never by letter — the letters join.

rules.name: Letter-spacing 0 on Persian text
rules.body: Letter-spacing 0 on Persian text , animated or not (§9).

rules.name: Invisible means unfocusable
rules.body: Invisible means unfocusable. Anything faded out that could take focus is made `inert`; decorative layers are `aria-hidden`.

rules.name: Anything that moves by itself can be stopped
rules.body: Anything that moves by itself can be stopped. The Work carousel is the one element that moves on its own: it pauses on hover, keyboard focus, off screen and while a card is turned over, carries a pause/play toggle, and never moves by itself under reduced motion. Its slide changes are CSS transitions of transform and opacity, written once per step; only its optional pointer tilt runs on the engine.

rules.name: Tools respond; they don't perform
rules.body: Tools respond; they don't perform. In the pricing calculator nothing is scroll-linked: tabs, tiles and toggle circles transition background and border over `--dur`, and a changed figure cross-fades (the old value up and out 8px, the new one in, 220ms; instant without `html.motion`). The sticky summary card and the bottom bar are plain CSS `position: sticky`. Keyboard focus scrolled into view clears the nav and the bar (`scroll-margin`).

dos: Use semantic tokens in components; primitives live only in `tokens.css`.
Keep one solid primary button per viewport.
Put project screenshots on the Work coverflow cards, and other mockups on forest tiles.
Use `#F1F5F2` for text on dark, and Persian digits in stats.
Pair every status color with an icon and words.
donts: Bring back navy, or any blue besides `info`.
Make anything green that can't be clicked (stats, hero chart bars, decorative icons on light).
Make buttons amber, or add gradients or glows to buttons.
Put mint or amber text on light backgrounds.
Use a forest card for paragraphs, or put a form on dark.
Use pure `#FFFFFF` as the page background or as text on dark.
Write raw hex values or Tailwind arbitrary colors (`bg-[#…]`) in components.
